items.question: Define the imaginary unit i and explain why it was introduced into mathematics. Then simplify √(-48) and express your answer in the form a + bi.

rubric.4: Defines i as √(-1) so i² = -1; explains it was introduced to solve equations like x² + 1 = 0; simplifies √(-48) = √(-1)·√(48) = i·4√3 = 4√3·i (or 0 + 4√3i)
rubric.3: Correct definition, explanation, and simplification with minor errors
rubric.2: Two of three components correct
rubric.1: One component correct

items.question: Given the complex numbers z₁ = 3 + 4i and z₂ = 2 - i. Part A: Calculate z₁ + z₂. Part B: Calculate z₁ · z₂. Part C: Find the modulus |z₁|. Part D: Explain the geometric meaning of the modulus.

rubric.4: A: 5 + 3i; B: (3+4i)(2-i) = 6 - 3i + 8i - 4i² = 6 + 5i + 4 = 10 + 5i; C: |z₁| = √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5; D: modulus is distance from origin to point (3,4) in complex plane
rubric.3: All parts correct with minor errors
rubric.2: Three parts correct
rubric.1: One or two parts correct

items.question: Prove that for any complex number z = a + bi, the product z · z̄ (where z̄ is the conjugate) equals |z|². Then use this to find the multiplicative inverse of 3 - 4i.

rubric.4: Proves z·z̄ = (a+bi)(a-bi) = a² - (bi)² = a² + b² = |z|²; uses this to find 1/(3-4i) = (3+4i)/((3-4i)(3+4i)) = (3+4i)/25 = 3/25 + (4/25)i
rubric.3: Complete proof and calculation with minor errors
rubric.2: Either proof or calculation complete
rubric.1: Attempts but significant errors in both

items.question: Explain why complex solutions to polynomial equations with real coefficients always come in conjugate pairs. Then find a quadratic equation with real coefficients that has 2 + 3i as one of its roots.

rubric.4: Explains: if a + bi is a root of p(x) with real coefficients, then p(a + bi) = 0; conjugating both sides (and using conjugate of sum/product properties) gives p(a - bi) = 0, so conjugate is also a root; constructs (x - (2+3i))(x - (2-3i)) = x² - 4x + 13
rubric.3: Correct explanation and equation with minor gaps
rubric.2: Either explanation or equation correct
rubric.1: Attempts but significant errors in both

items.question: Given that 1 - 2i is a root of x³ - 3x² + 7x - 5 = 0, find all three roots. Explain your strategy for finding the remaining roots.

rubric.4: Since coefficients are real, 1 + 2i is also a root; (x - (1-2i))(x - (1+2i)) = x² - 2x + 5; divides cubic by this to get x - 1; roots are 1 - 2i, 1 + 2i, and 1
rubric.3: Correct roots with adequate explanation of method
rubric.2: Finds some roots but strategy unclear or incomplete
rubric.1: Attempts but significant errors

items.question: Consider the rational function f(x) = (2x² - 8)/(x² - 4x + 3). Part A: Factor the numerator and denominator. Part B: Find any holes and vertical asymptotes. Part C: Find the horizontal asymptote. Part D: Sketch the graph showing all asymptotes and intercepts.

rubric.4: A: 2(x+2)(x-2)/((x-1)(x-3)); B: No holes (no common factors), VAs at x=1 and x=3; C: HA at y=2 (same degree, ratio of leading coefficients); D: Accurate sketch with all features labeled
rubric.3: All parts correct with minor errors
rubric.2: Three parts substantially correct
rubric.1: One or two parts correct

items.question: Graph f(x) = 2^(x-1) - 4. Identify the parent function, describe all transformations, find the horizontal asymptote, y-intercept, and any x-intercepts.

rubric.4: Parent: 2^x; Transformations: shift right 1, shift down 4; HA: y = -4; y-intercept: (0, 2^(-1) - 4) = (0, -3.5); x-intercept: solve 2^(x-1) = 4, x-1 = 2, x = 3, so (3, 0); accurate graph
rubric.3: All features identified with minor errors
rubric.2: Most features correct but some errors or incomplete
rubric.1: Some features correct but significant errors

items.question: Graph f(x) = log₂(x + 4) - 2 and its inverse function on the same coordinate plane. Describe the relationship between the two graphs and find where they intersect.

items.question: The function f(x) = x² is transformed to create g(x) = -2(x + 3)² + 5. Part A: Identify each transformation in order. Part B: Find the vertex and axis of symmetry of g(x). Part C: Determine the domain and range. Part D: Compare the graphs of f and g.

rubric.4: A: Shift left 3, vertical stretch by 2, reflect over x-axis, shift up 5; B: Vertex (-3, 5), axis of symmetry x = -3; C: Domain all reals, range (-∞, 5]; D: g is narrower than f, opens down instead of up, moved from (0,0) to (-3,5)
rubric.3: All parts correct with minor errors
rubric.2: Three parts substantially correct
rubric.1: One or two parts correct

items.question: Describe how to transform the graph of f(x) = ln(x) to obtain g(x) = ln(2 - x) + 1. Then determine the domain and range of g and find its x-intercept.

rubric.4: Transformations: reflect over y-axis to get ln(-x), shift right 2 to get ln(2-x), shift up 1; Domain: x < 2 (need 2-x > 0); Range: all reals; x-intercept: ln(2-x) + 1 = 0, ln(2-x) = -1, 2-x = e⁻¹, x = 2 - 1/e ≈ 1.63
rubric.3: All components correct with minor errors
rubric.2: Most transformations correct but domain/intercept errors
rubric.1: Some correct elements but significant errors

items.question: A function f(x) is even if f(-x) = f(x) and odd if f(-x) = -f(x). Determine whether g(x) = x³ - 4x is even, odd, or neither. Then prove that the product of two odd functions is an even function.

rubric.4: Shows g(-x) = (-x)³ - 4(-x) = -x³ + 4x = -(x³ - 4x) = -g(x), so g is odd; Proves: if f and h are odd, then (fh)(-x) = f(-x)h(-x) = (-f(x))(-h(x)) = f(x)h(x) = (fh)(x), so product is even
rubric.3: Both parts correct with minor gaps in proof
rubric.2: Classification correct, proof incomplete or vice versa
rubric.1: Attempts but significant errors in both

items.question: Convert 5π/4 radians to degrees. Then find the exact values of sin(5π/4), cos(5π/4), and tan(5π/4), using the unit circle. Explain which quadrant the angle is in and why the signs are what they are.

rubric.4: Converts: (5π/4)(180°/π) = 225°; In Quadrant III (between 180° and 270°); sin(5π/4) = -√2/2, cos(5π/4) = -√2/2, tan(5π/4) = 1; explains both x and y coordinates negative in QIII so sin and cos negative, tan positive
rubric.3: All values correct with adequate quadrant explanation
rubric.2: Conversion and values correct but weak explanation
rubric.1: Some values correct but significant errors

items.question: Explain why one radian is approximately 57.3°. Then derive a formula for the arc length s of a circle with radius r, where the central angle is θ radians. Use this to find the arc length when r = 10 cm and θ = 2.5 radians.

rubric.4: Explains: one radian is angle where arc length equals radius; since circumference = 2πr and full circle = 360°, 2π radians = 360°, so 1 radian = 360°/(2π) ≈ 57.3°; derives s = rθ from proportion; calculates s = 10(2.5) = 25 cm
rubric.3: All components correct with minor gaps
rubric.2: Two of three components correct
rubric.1: One component correct

items.question: A wheel has radius 2 feet and rotates at 150 revolutions per minute. Find the angular velocity in radians per second and the linear velocity of a point on the edge of the wheel in feet per second.

rubric.4: Angular velocity: 150 rev/min × (2π rad/rev) × (1 min/60 sec) = 5π rad/sec ≈ 15.7 rad/sec; Linear velocity: v = rω = 2 × 5π = 10π ft/sec ≈ 31.4 ft/sec
rubric.3: Both calculations correct with minor errors
rubric.2: One calculation correct
rubric.1: Attempts but significant unit conversion or formula errors

items.question: A sound wave is modeled by y = 3sin(440πt), where y is air pressure change and t is time in seconds. Find the frequency (cycles per second) and period. If another sound is modeled by y = 2sin(880πt), describe how these two sounds relate musically.

rubric.4: First wave: B = 440π, so ω = 440π, frequency = ω/(2π) = 220 Hz, period = 1/220 sec; Second wave: frequency = 440 Hz; explains second is exactly double frequency (one octave higher), with smaller amplitude (softer)

items.question: The depth of water in a harbor, in feet, is modeled by d(t) = 8sin(π/6 · t) + 12, where t is hours after midnight. Find the maximum and minimum depths, the times of high and low tide, and the period of the tidal cycle.

rubric.4: Max depth = 12 + 8 = 20 ft; Min depth = 12 - 8 = 4 ft; Period = 2π/(π/6) = 12 hours; High tide when sin = 1: t = 3, 15 (3am, 3pm); Low tide when sin = -1: t = 9, 21 (9am, 9pm)
rubric.3: All correct with minor errors
rubric.2: Most features correct but timing errors
rubric.1: Some correct but significant misunderstanding of sinusoidal model
